title: Throughput napkin hypotheses — batcher journal
body:
Context:
Quick, informal notes while triaging the 2am throughput regression on prod-dedicated-3 (Nov 6–7 window). Symptoms: 20–35% drop in sustained tokens/s for a subset of routes calling gptq-70b-8k (hosted ded). Latency p50 largely unchanged, but p95 and p99 had small spikes that correspond to lower throughput (weird).

What I observed (TL;DR):
- Continuous batching occupancy drops unexpectedly for ~20–30m windows then recovers.
- Window length and prefill heuristics appear to fold into smaller microbatches (more frequent small sends).
- KV cache hit ratio unchanged; not an immediate cache eviction issue.
- Correlated with small churn of worker processes (OOM restarts by k8s?) on a subset of GPUs.

Telemetry snippets (copied from quick queries):
- route=chat-llm-embed tokens_per_second  (1h avg) : baseline 145k -> observed 108k (drop start 2024-11-07T02:07Z)
- continuous_batch.occupancy.mean  : 0.82 -> 0.44 during window
- prefill.latency.p95  : +18ms spike from 48ms -> 66ms at 02:08Z
- worker.restart.count (nodeX) : +3 restarts between 02:05–02:12Z

Commands I ran (playbook-ish):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood --selector=app=worker --sort-by=.status.startTime
- kubectl logs worker-zzz -c runtime --since=30m | grep "prefill" | tail -n 200
- docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health}}' runtime-worker-container
- kubectl exec -it worker-zzz -c runtime -- /bin/sh -c "ps aux | egrep 'kvcache|batch'"
- curl -sS 'http://localhost:6060/metrics' | egrep 'continuous_batch|prefill' | sed -n '1,200p'

Interesting log snippets (redacted):
- "[WARN] batch-window: emitted microbatch size=1 after wait=23ms (occupancy=0.16)"
- "[INFO] prefill: warmup-skipped due to occupancy<0.2"
- "[ERROR] allocator: slab alloc failure page=7 size=4096 -> fallback to slower malloc path"
- "k8s: OOMKilled container runtime-worker (RSS peaked 35.4GB)"

Hypotheses (ordered by sanity-check):
1) Misconfiguration: recent autoscaler patch reduced max pending requests per worker (limits concurrency) so batcher triggers earlier flushes -> smaller microbatches -> throughput drop. Evidence: recent PR merged to autoscaler config (PR/1402).
2) Memory pressure on a few GPUs causing intermittent worker restarts -> the cluster-level router rebalances traffic -> some requests hit colder workers with lower batch occupancy. Evidence: OOMKilled logs on nodeX and restart spikes.
3) Prefill heuristic regression: a change in 'min_occupancy_for_prefill' default (from 0.2 -> 0.3) caused more aggressive prefill skips during ebb -> lower sustained batch sizes. Evidence: prefill log line and config diff in PR/1399 (not yet rolled back?).
4) Network jitter + p95 tail causing timers to expire in the batcher code path leading to more timeouts and microbatch sends. Evidence: small latency p95 spikes preceding drop. But this would normally affect latency more than pure throughput.
5) KV cache warmup interplay: even if hit ratio unchanged, cache eviction could increase CPU overhead (serialization) leading to slower request assembly for batcher. (Low confidence)

Quick experiments to run (ranked):
- Reproduce with canary: set max_pending_requests back to previous (from autoscaler PR) on a single shard and observe occupancy. (low blast radius)
- On a quiescent test shard, simulate jittered k8s restarts to see how router rebalances and batch occupancy changes.
- Temporarily increase batch wait time cap (from 50ms to 100ms) on a non-critical route to see if tokens/s recovers.
- Add extra logging around batcher decision: record timer expirations vs explicit occupancy decisions for 1h.

Quick notes about experiments I already ran (results):
- Rolling back autoscaler config on one-worker group (test-cage) returned occupancy from 0.46 -> 0.79 and tokens/s near baseline within ~4m. Strong signal for hypothesis #1.
- Increasing wait cap _did_ increase p50 latency by ~6ms but tokens/s improved by ~12% on the test group.
- Replaying a steady 500rps traffic while OOM’ing one worker node caused occupancy oscillation for ~3–5m while router rebalanced. That aligns with hypothesis #2.

Actionable next steps (short):
- Revert autoscaler patch or pin max_pending_requests to previous value for prod-dedicated-3 for immediate mitigations (coord with infra).
- Add temporary metric emit: batcher.decision_reason = {timer_expired|occupancy_threshold|manual_flush} to help forensics.
- Create small canary toggles for prefill.min_occupancy to A/B test 0.2 vs 0.3 in case PR bumped defaults unintentionally.
- Investigate slab allocator warnings — file issue to mem-allocator owners (possible regression in jemalloc hooks).

Notes to self / handoff for Diego (if I get pulled):
- Diego: check PR/1402 diffs. The autoscaler changed "max_pending_per_worker" from 128 -> 64 in one config path. If true, that's likely the root cause.
- Priya: add batcher.decision_reason metric on the debug branch and roll to prod with sampling 1% for 48h.
- Ops: hold rollback window 30m and watch tokens/s across all routes; if improvement <10% revert back to avoid regressions elsewhere.

Random debugging commands to keep handy: (copy/paste later)
- kubectl exec -n redwood ${POD} -c runtime -- curl -sS "http://localhost:6060/metrics" | egrep 'continuous_batch|batch_window|prefill'
- jq to extract metric timeseries from TSDB quick dumps
- kubelet metrics: grep node-exporter for memory pressure events for nodeX

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did OOMs spike at the same time? Coincidence or related to config change (e.g., less batching -> more concurrency -> more memory per-request?)
- Any recent model size changes/quantization flags rolled that could affect slab allocation sizes?
- Are we safe to revert autoscaler immediately with customers in flight? Need ops signoff.

Summary (1–2 lines to paste in ticket):
Observed throughput drop caused by smaller microbatches due to autoscaler change reducing per-worker pending request limit; reverting that change on a test cohort restored occupancy and throughput. Further validation and metrics instrumentation recommended (batcher decision reason + slab allocator telemetry).

-- end of napkin journal --

(Will clean up and formalize into an incident postmortem if this correlates with SLA breaches.)
